subject: math
title: Math Book — enVision Florida B.E.S.T. Grade 6
intro: This follows your real math book. Tap the topic you're working on in class, read the lesson, watch the video, then print the worksheet and practice!

lessons.title: Fluently add, subtract, and multiply decimals
lessons.teach: Line up the decimal points, then add or subtract like normal. To multiply, ignore the decimals, multiply the digits, then count the total decimal places to place the point.

lessons.title: Fluently divide whole numbers and decimals
lessons.teach: When dividing by a decimal, move the decimal point in the divisor to make it a whole number, move it the same number of places in the dividend, then divide.

lessons.title: Multiply fractions
lessons.teach: Multiply the top numbers (numerators) together and the bottom numbers (denominators) together, then simplify. No common denominator needed!

lessons.title: Understand division with fractions
lessons.teach: Dividing asks 'how many groups fit?' Dividing by a fraction means flipping it (its reciprocal) and multiplying instead.

lessons.title: Divide fractions by fractions
lessons.teach: Keep the first fraction, Change divide to multiply, and Flip the second fraction (Keep-Change-Flip). Then multiply across.

lessons.title: Divide mixed numbers
lessons.teach: First turn each mixed number into an improper fraction, then use Keep-Change-Flip just like dividing regular fractions.

lessons.title: Solve problems with rational numbers
lessons.teach: Read the word problem carefully, decide which operation it's asking for, then add, subtract, multiply, or divide your decimals and fractions to solve.

lessons.title: Understand integers
lessons.teach: Integers are whole numbers and their opposites: …-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3… Negative numbers are less than zero (like temperatures below freezing or money owed).

lessons.title: Represent rational numbers on the number line
lessons.teach: Any number you can write as a fraction is rational. Plot them on a number line — negatives to the left of zero, positives to the right.

lessons.title: Absolute values of rational numbers
lessons.teach: Absolute value is a number's distance from zero, so it's always positive. |-5| = 5 and |5| = 5 because both are 5 steps from zero.

lessons.title: Add integers
lessons.teach: Same signs: add and keep the sign. Different signs: subtract and take the sign of the bigger number. Think of gaining and losing.

lessons.title: Subtract integers
lessons.teach: Subtracting is adding the opposite: a - b = a + (-b). Keep-Change-Change, then follow the adding rules.

lessons.title: Multiply integers
lessons.teach: Two same signs make a positive; two different signs make a negative. (-)(-) = +, (-)(+) = -.

lessons.title: Divide integers
lessons.teach: Same sign rule as multiplying: same signs give a positive answer, different signs give a negative answer.

lessons.title: Solve problems with absolute value
lessons.teach: Use absolute value when a question asks 'how far' or 'how much', like distance or temperature change — the answer is always positive.

lessons.title: Understand, represent, and evaluate exponents
lessons.teach: An exponent tells how many times to multiply the base by itself. 2^4 = 2×2×2×2 = 16. The small number is the exponent.

lessons.title: Find the greatest common factor
lessons.teach: The GCF is the largest number that divides evenly into two numbers. List the factors of each (or use prime factors) and pick the biggest one they share.

lessons.title: Write and evaluate numerical expressions
lessons.teach: Follow the order of operations (PEMDAS): Parentheses, Exponents, Multiply/Divide left to right, then Add/Subtract left to right.

lessons.title: Write algebraic expressions
lessons.teach: Turn words into math with a variable (a letter for the unknown). 'Five more than a number' becomes n + 5.

lessons.title: Evaluate algebraic expressions
lessons.teach: Substitute the given value in for the variable, then use order of operations to find the answer. If x = 3, then 2x + 1 = 2(3) + 1 = 7.

lessons.title: Apply properties of operations
lessons.teach: The distributive property lets you multiply across a sum: 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12. Properties help you rewrite expressions in easier forms.

lessons.title: Simplify algebraic expressions
lessons.teach: Combine like terms (terms with the same variable). 4x + 2x = 6x. Only combine terms that match.

topics.title: Represent and Solve Equations and Inequalities

lessons.title: Understand equations and solutions
lessons.teach: An equation says two things are equal (has an = sign). A solution is the value of the variable that makes it true.

lessons.title: Apply properties of equality
lessons.teach: Whatever you do to one side of an equation, do to the other side too — that keeps it balanced.

lessons.title: Write and solve addition and subtraction equations
lessons.teach: To solve x + 7 = 12, do the opposite operation: subtract 7 from both sides to get x = 5.

lessons.title: Write and solve multiplication and division equations
lessons.teach: To solve 4x = 20, divide both sides by 4 to get x = 5. Use the opposite operation to undo it.

lessons.title: Write and solve equations with rational numbers
lessons.teach: Same balancing rules work with fractions and decimals — do the opposite operation to both sides to isolate the variable.

lessons.title: Understand and write inequalities
lessons.teach: Inequalities compare with >, <, ≥, or ≤ instead of =. 'At least 10' means x ≥ 10.

lessons.title: Represent solutions to inequalities
lessons.teach: Graph on a number line: open circle for > or <, closed circle for ≥ or ≤, then shade the side that makes it true.

topics.title: Understand and Use Ratio and Rate

lessons.title: Understand ratios
lessons.teach: A ratio compares two amounts. 3 cats to 2 dogs can be written 3:2, 3 to 2, or 3/2.

lessons.title: Generate equivalent ratios
lessons.teach: Multiply or divide BOTH numbers by the same value to get an equal ratio. 3:2 = 6:4 = 9:6.

lessons.title: Compare ratios
lessons.teach: Make the ratios have a common term (or find unit rates), then compare. A ratio table helps line them up.

lessons.title: Represent and graph ratios
lessons.teach: Equivalent ratios form a straight line through the origin when graphed as ordered pairs.

lessons.title: Understand rates and unit rates
lessons.teach: A rate compares two different units (miles per hour). A unit rate is the amount for ONE unit — divide to find it.

lessons.title: Compare unit rates
lessons.teach: Find each unit rate (price per item, miles per hour), then the better deal is usually the lower cost or higher speed per unit.

lessons.title: Solve unit rate problems
lessons.teach: Once you know the unit rate, multiply to scale up to any amount you need.

lessons.title: Ratio reasoning: convert customary units
lessons.teach: Use a conversion ratio (like 12 inches = 1 foot) and multiply so the units you don't want cancel out.

lessons.title: Ratio reasoning: convert metric units
lessons.teach: Metric units change by powers of 10. Move the decimal point — for example 1 meter = 100 centimeters.

lessons.title: Understand percent
lessons.teach: Percent means 'per 100.' 25% means 25 out of 100, which is the same as 25/100 or 0.25.

lessons.title: Relate fractions, decimals, and percents
lessons.teach: Move between forms: 1/2 = 0.5 = 50%. Divide a fraction to get a decimal, multiply by 100 to get a percent.

lessons.title: Represent percents greater than 100 or less than 1
lessons.teach: 150% means more than the whole (1.5). Half a percent (0.5%) is a tiny amount, 0.005 as a decimal.

lessons.title: Estimate to find percent
lessons.teach: Use friendly percents to estimate: 10% is easy (move the decimal), and you can build others like 5% (half of 10%) or 20% (double 10%).

lessons.title: Find the percent of a number
lessons.teach: Change the percent to a decimal and multiply. 20% of 60 = 0.20 × 60 = 12.

lessons.title: Find the whole given the part and the percent
lessons.teach: Divide the part by the percent (as a decimal). If 12 is 20%, then the whole is 12 ÷ 0.20 = 60.

topics.title: Model and Solve Problems Involving Geometry

lessons.title: Represent rational numbers on the coordinate plane
lessons.teach: The plane has 4 quadrants. An ordered pair (x, y) tells you to go right/left then up/down from the origin (0,0).

lessons.title: Solve problems on the coordinate plane
lessons.teach: To find distance along the same line, subtract the coordinates (or count units). Plot points to find perimeter or area of a shape.

lessons.title: Derive and apply the triangle area formula
lessons.teach: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. A triangle is half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

lessons.title: Decompose polygons into triangles and rectangles
lessons.teach: Break a complex shape into rectangles and triangles, find each area, then add them up.

lessons.title: Represent solid figures using nets
lessons.teach: A net is a flattened-out 3D shape. Unfold a box and you see all its faces — that's its net.

lessons.title: Find surface areas of prisms
lessons.teach: Surface area is the total area of all the faces. Find the area of each face on the net and add them together.
lessons.videoTitle: Surface Area of a Rectangular Prism

lessons.title: Find surface areas of pyramids
lessons.teach: Add the area of the base to the areas of all the triangular faces using the net.

lessons.title: Find volume with fractional edge lengths
lessons.teach: Volume of a rectangular prism = length × width × height. It works even when the edges are fractions or decimals.

lessons.title: Recognize statistical questions
lessons.teach: A statistical question has answers that vary (like 'How tall are the students?'). 'How tall am I?' is not statistical — it has one answer.

lessons.title: Summarize data using mean, median, mode, and range
lessons.teach: Mean is the average, median is the middle, mode is the most common, and range is the highest minus the lowest.

lessons.title: Describe and interpret line plots
lessons.teach: A line plot uses Xs above a number line to show how often each value appears — great for spotting clusters and gaps.

lessons.title: Display data in frequency tables and histograms
lessons.teach: A histogram groups data into equal intervals (bins) and uses bars to show how many fall in each range.

lessons.title: Display data in box plots
lessons.teach: A box plot shows the five-number summary: minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, and maximum. The box is the middle half of the data.

lessons.title: Determine how data changes impact statistical measures
lessons.teach: Adding or changing a value can shift the mean, median, or range. Outliers pull the mean the most.
